scope: Source inspection only; no external implementation executed

code_sources.observation: OLMoE n-token path loops over active experts and invokes three quantized GEMMs per active expert. Single-token path uses fused expert projections.
Already implements variable-M mixed-bit grouped GEMM, fused gate/up activation, deterministic full and chunk reductions.

Each call visits slots in ascending order, but masks out assignments outside that expert-sorted chunk and carries a FP32 accumulator between chunks. This alone does not preserve global slot order across chunk sizes.
Randomized 19-token combine test checks FP16 equality to a reference. No inference about all inputs follows from that finite test.

Documents workspace chunking and numerical tolerance. Its public chunk_tokens option is multiplied by top_k to obtain an assignment limit. Does not establish a promise of bitwise invariance across chunk settings.
Existing batch-invariant BF16 grouped-GEMM wrapper and rounding-aware MoE helpers; broad MoE determinism is not an untouched topic.
Verified deterministic serving engine; README lists MoE as unsupported. Missing support alone is not evidence of research novelty.

primary_literature.finding: Hardware-aware mixed precision allocation and heterogeneous Group-GEMM generation already address precision-dependent scheduling.
Routing-distribution-aware kernel dispatch already exists; no general adaptive-dispatch novelty claim.
Quantized MoE decode launch/padding overhead already targeted by persistent fused execution; H200 results not a 4090 baseline.
Existing low-precision MoE consistency work aligns quantization, GEMMs and merge order. No claim that quantized MoE consistency is new.
System-level deterministic inference formalized and verified; MoE expansion is discussed explicitly.
Kernel-checker adequacy/mutation analysis already investigated; moving to GPU validation does not by itself establish a novel topic.

limitations: No independent reproduction of published speedups
CPU scalar arithmetic emulates the reviewed merge order but is not CUDA execution
No model-quality or runtime-speedup result from this review
